Sherlock Holmes corresponds to Kyoichiro Kaga: Both are the main detective characters in detective novels, known for their keen observation and excellent reasoning ability.

Reasoning and puzzle solving correspond to psychological description and narrative: In "The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes," reasoning and puzzle solving are the core elements of the work, and the story revolves around Sherlock Holmes solving cases one by one; in "Naoko," psychological description and narrative are one of the characteristics of the work, through in-depth exploration of the characters' inner world, it shows the complexity of human nature and the twists and turns of the story. Although these two sets of concepts have differences to some extent, they are both important components in their respective works, shaping the unique style of each work.

Holmes's popularity is such that many believe him to be a genuine person, not a fictional hero. His impact on popular culture and mystery writing cannot be understated, with countless adaptations and recreations appearing in literature, television, film, video games, and other media.
